ShouldRetry.description:
Whether the condition behind this error may clear, so that retrying the request could
succeed. true marks a transient failure such as missing capacity, a rate limit, or a
creation still in progress: retry after Retry-After when present, otherwise with
exponential backoff. false marks a failure a retry cannot fix, such as a malformed request
or a configuration fault, or an outcome that is unknown, where a retry could create a
second sandbox. Successful responses and errors without an explicit classification omit
the header. With idempotency enabled, retry sandbox creation with the same Idempotency-Key
and request parameters. A retryable creation failure permits a fresh attempt; an
idempotency_in_progress response only reports an existing attempt and never releases it.

memory.description: Defaults to true. When false and the sandbox is paused, resume from disk state only: the sandbox cold-boots fresh and any memory in the snapshot is ignored, never modified or deleted. Disk state has crash-recovery semantics — writes not flushed before the pause may be lost. A no-op for snapshots that contain no memory. Rejected with an error in environments where this capability is not enabled, never silently downgraded to a memory restore. A snapshot taken while the sandbox guest agent was not responding (envdUnresponsiveAtPause) can only be resumed this way, and needs no enablement.

SandboxEgressProxyConfig.description: SOCKS5 proxy for sandbox egress. Outbound TCP is tunneled through the proxy after allow/deny filtering; the sandbox is unaware. Domain-matched flows use remote DNS (ATYP=domain).

address.description: SOCKS5 proxy address in host:port format (e.g. "proxy.example.com:1080").

SandboxEgressProxyTLSConfig.description: TLS for the connection to the SOCKS5 proxy. The SOCKS5 negotiation and the tunneled traffic both run inside the TLS session, so the proxy credentials are not sent in the clear. This secures only the hop to the proxy; what the proxy does onward is its own concern. A half-close from the sandbox reaches the proxy as a TLS close_notify, not a TCP FIN, and a proxy that treats close_notify as a full close cuts the reply short.

caCert.description: One or more PEM-encoded certificates to verify the proxy against, for a proxy fronted by a private CA. These replace the system trust store, which is what is used when this is omitted. The system trust store depends on the host the orchestrator runs on, so set this to get the same verification everywhere.

enabled.description: Connect to the proxy over TLS. When false, no other field in this object may be set.

serverName.description: Name to verify the proxy certificate against, and to send as SNI. Defaults to the host part of address. Set this only when the certificate does not match the address the proxy is reached at.

allowOut.description: List of allowed destinations for egress traffic. Each entry can be a CIDR block (e.g. "8.8.8.8/32"), a bare IP address (e.g. "8.8.8.8"), or a domain name (e.g. "example.com", "*.example.com"). Allowed entries always take precedence over denied entries. When allowOut contains a domain, the servers in dnsServers (8.8.8.8 by default) are also allowed.

allowPublicTraffic.description: Whether sandbox URLs accept traffic without the sandbox's traffic access token. When omitted or null on create, the project's default applies, which is true unless the project changed it.

dnsServers.description: DNS servers the sandbox can reach when allowOut contains a domain. Each entry must be an IPv4 address, and all traffic to it is allowed. Omit it to allow the default nameserver 8.8.8.8, or pass an empty list to allow none. This does not change the sandbox's /etc/resolv.conf.

httpsPorts.description: Sandbox ports that serve HTTPS rather than plaintext HTTP. Affects how the proxy reaches the service inside the sandbox; the public URL is HTTPS either way. Certificates are not verified, so self-signed ones work. The envd port (49983) cannot be listed.

maskRequestHost.description: Specify host mask which will be used for all sandbox requests

rules.description: Per-domain transform rules applied to matching outbound HTTPS requests. Keys may be exact DNS names (for example, "api.example.com") or a leading wildcard (for example, "*.example.com"), and are normalized to lowercase on write. Wildcards match subdomains at any depth but not the apex domain; a bare "*" is invalid. Exact rules take precedence, followed by the longest matching wildcard suffix, and matching rule sets are not merged. Broad wildcards such as "*.com" are allowed and may expose transformed credentials to every matching destination the sandbox contacts. Rules do not grant network access; configure allowOut separately to permit the destination.

parameters.description:
Optional team-scoped key for retrying sandbox creation. Use 1 to 255 lowercase ASCII
letters, digits, or hyphens (a-z, 0-9, -), such as a lowercase UUID. When idempotency is enabled,
matching retries replay a completed status and body for the retention period. A creation
failure explicitly classified as safe to retry (Should-Retry: true) permits a fresh
attempt with the same key and parameters. Only one attempt can run at a time.
Different request parameters return 409 with error_code idempotency_request_mismatch.
An in-progress request returns 409 with error_code idempotency_in_progress; an unknown
outcome returns 422 with error_code idempotency_outcome_unknown. These retries do not execute the request again.
Retries do not extend retention. If a fresh attempt's request deadline plus response
persistence budget would exceed the remaining retention, the previous error is replayed.
After the key expires, it can start a new creation.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: The Idempotency-Key conflicts with a different request (error_code idempotency_request_mismatch), or the matching original request has no recorded response yet and is within its expected response window (error_code idempotency_in_progress); this request was not executed again

422.description: The matching original request has no recorded response and its expected response deadline has passed or is unknown (error_code idempotency_outcome_unknown); this request was not executed again

Retry-After.description: When present, the number of seconds to wait before retrying the request.
